title: The Belmont Report & Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)
description: Master the three core ethical pillars—Respect for Persons, Beneficence, and Justice—and learn how IRBs evaluate research risk.

slides.title: The Triad of the Belmont Report (1979) 🏛️
slides.content:
# The Constitutional Framework of Research Ethics

In 1979, the National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects of Biomedical and Behavioral Research published the **Belmont Report**, which defines three foundational ethical principles:

1. **Respect for Persons**: Individuals must be treated as autonomous agents capable of self-determination. Those with diminished autonomy (e.g., children, prisoners, individuals with cognitive impairments) are entitled to special protection.
2. **Beneficence**: Researchers must maximize potential benefits while minimizing potential risks of harm (*'Do no harm'* and conduct thorough risk-benefit analyses).
3. **Justice**: Fair distribution of both the burdens and the benefits of research. Vulnerable or marginalized populations must not be exploited simply because they are easily accessible.

quizData.question: A pharmaceutical company tests a risky new antidepressant exclusively on low-income psychiatric patients, but intends to market the drug exclusively to wealthy private clinics. Which Belmont principle is violated?
quizData.explanation: The principle of Justice requires that the group bearing the burdens and risks of research must also share in its eventual benefits.

slides.title: Institutional Review Boards (IRB) 🛡️
slides.content:
## Who Evaluates Research Proposals?

An **Institutional Review Board (IRB)** is an independent multidisciplinary committee mandated by federal law to review and approve all research involving human participants before data collection can begin.

| Level of IRB Review | Risk Threshold | Example Research Protocols |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Exempt Review** | Less than minimal risk | Anonymous surveys, analysis of de-identified public datasets, standard educational tests. |
| **Expedited Review** | Minimal risk (no greater than risks encountered in daily life or routine physical exams) | Non-invasive physiological recordings (heart rate, EEG), recording healthy voice samples. |
| **Full Board Review** | Greater than minimal risk or involves vulnerable groups | Experimental manipulation of acute stress, invasive drugs, deception, research on prisoners or children. |

Researchers cannot self-certify that their study is exempt; only the IRB makes that determination.

quizData.question: A graduate student designs an online anonymous survey investigating sleep patterns and coffee consumption in healthy adults. What level of IRB review does this typically require?

options.text: Full Board Review by 10 senior physicians
Criminal background check by state police
No ethics compliance check of any kind

quizData.explanation: Anonymous educational or behavioral surveys with adult participants presenting less than minimal risk qualify for an Exempt IRB determination.

slides.title: Ethical Warning ⚠️
slides.content:
### Never Collect Data Prior to IRB Approval

Collecting a single data point from a human participant before formal written IRB approval is a severe compliance violation. Federal regulators can halt all research funding at an entire university if unapproved data collection occurs!
